# Godot — Deprecated APIs

Last verified: 2026-10-17 (4.7 rows); 2026-02-12 (rest)

The 4.7 migration guide lists no formal deprecations; the 4.7 rows below are
renames and removals from it
(https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html).

If an agent suggests any API in the "Deprecated" column, it MUST be replaced
with the "Use Instead" column.

## Nodes & Classes

| Deprecated | Use Instead | Since | Notes |
|------------|-------------|-------|-------|
| `TileMap` | `TileMapLayer` | 4.3 | One node per layer instead of multi-layer node |
| `VisibilityNotifier2D` | `VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D` | 4.0 | Renamed for clarity |
| `VisibilityNotifier3D` | `VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D` | 4.0 | Renamed for clarity |
| `YSort` | `Node2D.y_sort_enabled` | 4.0 | Property on Node2D, not a separate node |
| `Navigation2D` / `Navigation3D` | `NavigationServer2D` / `NavigationServer3D` | 4.0 | Server-based API |
| `EditorSceneFormatImporterFBX` | `EditorSceneFormatImporterFBX2GLTF` | 4.3 | Renamed |

## Methods & Properties

| Deprecated | Use Instead | Since | Notes |
|------------|-------------|-------|-------|
| `yield()` | `await signal` | 4.0 | GDScript 2.0 coroutine syntax |
| `connect("signal", obj, "method")` | `signal.connect(callable)` | 4.0 | Callable-based connections |
| `instance()` | `instantiate()` | 4.0 | Renamed |
| `PackedScene.instance()` | `PackedScene.instantiate()` | 4.0 | Renamed |
| `get_world()` | `get_world_3d()` | 4.0 | Explicit 2D/3D split |
| `OS.get_ticks_msec()` | `Time.get_ticks_msec()` | 4.0 | Time singleton preferred |
| `duplicate()` for nested resources | `duplicate_deep()` | 4.5 | Explicit deep copy control |
| `Skeleton3D` signal `bone_pose_updated` | `skeleton_updated` | 4.3 | Renamed |
| `AnimationPlayer.method_call_mode` | `AnimationMixer.callback_mode_method` | 4.3 | Moved to base class |
| `AnimationPlayer.playback_active` | `AnimationMixer.active` | 4.3 | Moved to base class |
| `RichTextLabel.ImageUpdateMask.UPDATE_WIDTH_IN_PERCENT` | `ImageUpdateMask.UPDATE_WIDTH_UNIT` | 4.7 | Renamed; GDScript using the old name breaks |
| `add_image()` / `update_image()` `width_in_percent`, `height_in_percent` (`bool`) | `width_unit`, `height_unit` (`RichTextLabel.ImageUnit`) | 4.7 | Renamed and retyped |
| `DisplayServer.AccessibilityLiveMode` for `Control.accessibility_live` | `AccessibilityServer.AccessibilityLiveMode` | 4.7 | Enum moved to `AccessibilityServer` |
| `AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.tap_back_pos` | — | 4.7 | Removed |
| `EditorSceneFormatImporter.IMPORT_*` constants | `EditorSceneFormatImporter.ImportFlags` enum | 4.7 | Same names, now in an enum |

## Patterns (Not Just APIs)

| Deprecated Pattern | Use Instead | Why |
|--------------------|-------------|-----|
| String-based `connect()` | Typed signal connections | Type-safe, refactor-friendly |
| `$NodePath` in `_process()` | `@onready var` cached reference | Performance: path lookup every frame |
| Untyped `Array` / `Dictionary` | `Array[Type]`, typed variables | GDScript compiler optimizations |
| `Texture2D` in `Shader.set_default_texture_parameter()` / `get_default_texture_parameter()` | `Texture` base type | Changed in 4.4; the shading language's `sampler2D` / `texture()` did not change |
| Manual post-process viewport chains | `Compositor` + `CompositorEffect` | Structured post-processing (4.3+) |
| GodotPhysics3D for new projects | Jolt Physics 3D | Default since 4.6; better stability |
| `event.device == 0` to detect mouse or keyboard | `event is InputEventMouse` / `InputEventKey`, or `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` / `DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD` | Since 4.7 mouse and keyboard no longer report device `0`, which some joypads use |
| Installing addons from the editor's AssetLib tab | The editor's Asset Store workspace (4.7+) | 4.7 replaced the Asset Library with the Asset Store |
# Godot — Current Best Practices

Last verified: 2026-10-17 (4.7 sections); 2026-02-12 (rest) | Engine: Godot 4.7

Practices that are **new or changed** since the model's training data (~4.3).
This supplements (not replaces) the agent's built-in knowledge.

## GDScript (4.5+)

- **Variadic arguments**: Functions can accept arbitrary parameter counts. The
  rest parameter is written `...name`, comes last, and is typed `Array` or left
  untyped — `values: Variant...` and `...values: Array[int]` do not parse
  ```gdscript
  func log_values(prefix: String, ...values: Array) -> void:
      for v in values:
          print(prefix, ": ", v)
  ```

- **Lambdas capture local variables by value** (every Godot 4 version): a local
  is captured once, when the lambda is created, and a lambda cannot reassign an
  outer local — `var hit := false` / `func(): hit = true` leaves the caller's
  `hit` false. Share state through a reference type (a Dictionary, an Array or
  an object) and mutate its contents. A rest parameter works in a lambda too, so
  `func(...args)` connects to a signal with any number of arguments (observed on
  4.6.1; a one-argument lambda on a zero-argument signal errors "Method expected
  1 argument(s), but called with 0")
  ```gdscript
  var state := {"emitted": false}
  some_signal.connect(func(...args): state.emitted = true)
  ```

- **Abstract classes and methods**: Use `@abstract` to enforce inheritance
  ```gdscript
  @abstract
  class_name BaseEnemy extends CharacterBody3D

  # No body: "a newline or a semicolon is expected after the function header".
  # Subclasses MUST override it.
  @abstract func get_attack_pattern() -> Array[Attack]
  ```

- **Script backtracing**: Detailed call stacks available even in Release builds

## GDScript (4.7)

- **An override of a typed method inherits its return type**, so it needs an
  explicit `return` statement; the migration guide's fix is `return null`
- **Writing one element of a packed array no longer calls the property's
  setter.** A setter on a `PackedInt32Array` (etc.) property no longer runs on
  `arr[i] = v`; assign the whole array where the setter has to run

## Physics (4.7)

- **Jolt `WorldBoundaryShape3D`**: the sign of `plane.d` now matches Godot
  Physics, flipped from 4.6. Negate it in scenes authored on 4.6
- **Jolt `SoftBody3D`**: mass is 1 kg for the whole body (was 1 kg per point)
  and `linear_stiffness` is applied differently; re-tune `linear_stiffness`
  and `damping_coefficient`. `Area3D` now reports `SoftBody3D` overlaps
- **Audio areas**: `area_mask` on `AudioStreamPlayer2D`/`3D` defaults to `0`
  (was layer `1`); set it to layer `1` where `audio_bus_override` areas are used

## Physics (4.6)

- **Jolt Physics is the default 3D engine** for new projects
  - Better determinism and stability than GodotPhysics3D
  - Some HingeJoint3D properties (`damp`) only work with GodotPhysics
  - Switch: Project Settings → Physics → 3D → Physics Engine
  - 2D physics unchanged (still Godot Physics 2D)

## Rendering (4.7)

- **`AreaLight3D`**: real-time rectangular area lights, instead of an emissive
  material plus global illumination
- **HDR output** on Windows, macOS, iOS, visionOS and Linux (Wayland)
- **`DrawableTexture2D`**: a simpler API for drawing onto textures
- **`CanvasItem` lines are drawn without an antialiasing feather**, so they look
  thinner than in 4.6; widen lines that relied on the old look
- The `LinearToSRGB` visual shader node no longer clamps to `[0.0, 1.0]` under
  Forward+ and Mobile

## Rendering (4.6)

- **D3D12 is the default backend on Windows** (was Vulkan) — for better driver compatibility
- **Glow now processes before tonemapping** with screen blending mode — existing glow setups may look different
- **SSR overhauled** — significant improvement in realism, stability, and performance
- **AgX tonemapper** — new white point and contrast controls

## Rendering (4.5)

- **Shader Baker**: Pre-compile shaders to eliminate startup hitching
- **SMAA 1x**: New AA option — sharper than FXAA, cheaper than TAA
- **Stencil buffer**: Available for advanced masking/portal effects
- **Bent normal maps**: Directional occlusion in normal map textures
- **Specular occlusion**: Ambient occlusion now affects reflections

## Accessibility (4.5+)

- **Screen reader support**: Control nodes integrate with accessibility tools via AccessKit
- **Live translation preview**: Test GUI layouts in different languages directly in-editor
- **FoldableContainer**: New accordion-style UI node for collapsible sections
- **Recursive Control disable**: Disable mouse/focus interactions for entire node hierarchies with a single property

## Animation (4.5+)

- **BoneConstraint3D**: Bind bones to other bones with modifiers
  - AimModifier3D, CopyTransformModifier3D, ConvertTransformModifier3D

## Animation (4.7)

- **`Tween.tween_await()`** pauses a tween until a signal is emitted
- **`LookAtModifier3D.relative`** defaults to `false` (was `true`)

## Animation (4.6)

- **IK system fully restored**: Complete inverse kinematics reintroduced for 3D
  - Available modifiers: CCDIK, FABRIK, Jacobian IK, Spline IK, TwoBoneIK
  - Applied via `SkeletonModifier3D` nodes

## Resources (4.5+)

- **`duplicate_deep()`**: Explicit deep duplication for nested resource trees
  - Old `duplicate()` behavior retained for backward compatibility
  - Use `duplicate_deep()` when you need per-instance copies of nested resources

## Navigation (4.5+)

- **Dedicated 2D navigation server**: No longer proxied through 3D NavigationServer
  - Reduces export binary size for 2D-only games

## UI (4.6)

- **Dual-focus system**: Mouse/touch focus is now separate from keyboard/gamepad focus
  - Visual feedback differs depending on input method
  - Consider this when designing custom focus behavior

## UI and Input (4.7)

- **`Control.offset_transform_*`** (`offset_transform_enabled`,
  `offset_transform_position`, `offset_transform_rotation`,
  `offset_transform_scale`, …): a visual transform that containers do not
  reset, for hover and press animations inside containers
- **`RichTextLabel` images can size relative to the font**
  (`[img height=1em]…[/img]`); `add_image()` / `update_image()` take
  `width_unit` / `height_unit` (`RichTextLabel.ImageUnit`) in place of the
  `*_in_percent` booleans
- **`VirtualJoystick` node** for touch controls, with Fixed, Dynamic and
  Following modes
- **Mouse and keyboard events report `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` /
  `DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`**, not device `0`; check the event type rather than
  `device == 0`
- **New projects stretch by default**: `display/window/stretch/mode` is
  `canvas_items` and `aspect` is `expand`. Projects created before 4.7 keep
  their settings

## Editor Workflow (4.7)

- **The Asset Store replaces the Asset Library**: the editor workspace is
  "Asset Store" (it was "AssetLib"), and addons such as gdUnit4 are installed
  from there
- Method, signal and property names show in a monospace font by default
  ("Use Monospace Font for Editor Symbols" turns it off)

## Editor Workflow (4.6)

- Flexible dock drag-and-drop with blue outline preview (including bottom panel)
- Most panels support floating windows (except Debugger)
- New keyboard shortcuts: Alt+O (Output), Alt+S (Shader)
- Export variable auto-generation: drag resource from FileSystem into script editor
- Live preview in Quick Open dialog when "Live Preview" enabled
- New "Select Mode" (v key) prevents accidental transforms; old mode renamed "Transform Mode" (q key)

## Tooling

- **ripgrep has no `gdscript` type**: `*.gd` is registered under `gap` (GAP programming language).
  `rg --type gdscript` is a hard error — the search never executes.
  Always use `rg --glob "*.gd"` (shell) or `glob: "*.gd"` (Grep tool) to filter GDScript files.

## Command Line — Tests and Parse Check

Flags, from Godot's command-line tutorial: `--headless` (headless display and a
dummy audio driver, "useful for servers and with `--script`"), `--path <dir>`
(a directory holding `project.godot`), `-s`/`--script <script>`, `-d`/`--debug`
(the local stdout debugger), `--remote-debug <protocol>://<host>[:<port>]`,
`--import` (starts the editor, waits for the import, and quits),
`--quit-after <n>` (iterations), `--export-debug <preset>` (implies `--import`)
and `--check-only` (parse for errors and quit, with `--script`). The editor is
not on `PATH` by default: on Windows and Linux run the binary by its relative or
absolute path; on macOS run `Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot` inside the bundle.

gdUnit4's runner is `res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd`; `-a <dir|suite>`
adds suites, reports go to `res://reports/` by default (`-rd` changes it), and
the documented exit codes are 0 (all passed), 100 (failures) and 101 (warnings).
The command the framework uses:
`godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`.

gdUnit4 6.2.x lists Godot 4.5 to 4.7.1 as compatible in its README
(https://github.com/godot-gdunit-labs/gdUnit4#compatibility-overview, checked
2026-10-17); 4.7.2 is not listed there yet, but gdUnit4 6.2.2 runs on it. On
Windows, 2026-10-17, Godot 4.7.2 and 4.7.1 gave the same exits on the command
above: 0 pass, 100 fail, 101 orphans, 105 parse error, 0 with `No test cases
found` over none, and 1 before the first import.

Observed on Godot 4.6.1 with gdUnit4 6.1.3, and the exits again on 4.7.2 with
6.2.2 — not in the docs:
- 101 is also the exit when every test passed but a test leaked orphan nodes;
  105 means a test script does not parse; 103 means gdUnit4 refused to run
  headless (`--ignoreHeadlessMode` missing). 104 is gdUnit4 refusing a Godot
  older than 4.3 — not reproducible on the pin.
- Over zero tests the runner prints `No test cases found` and exits 0.
- Without `--remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0`, a script error opens the `-d`
  debugger and the run waits at a `debug>` prompt; with it, every run prints two
  `ERROR:` lines about the remote port, which are expected.
- A fresh clone has no `.godot/` class cache: run
  `godot --headless --path . --import` first, or `GdUnitCmdTool.gd` does not
  load and the run exits 1 having run nothing.
- On 4.7.1 and 4.7.2 (Windows, 2026-10-17), that first `--import` of a fresh
  project crashed on exit (139, segmentation fault) in 3 of 17 runs, after
  writing the same `.godot/` files as a clean run; running it again exited 0.
  4.6.1 did not crash in 4 runs.
- `--check-only` with `-s <file>` exits 1 on valid code that names an autoload
  (`Identifier not found`), and `--import` / `--quit-after` exit 0 on a parse
  error — neither is a parse check. The framework's parse check is
  `godot --headless --path . -s res://.claude/scripts/godot-parse-check.gd -- res://<file>.gd …`
  (exit 1 when a script does not load).
- On Windows, a quoted full path to the editor (`"C:/Program Files/Godot/…exe"`)
  runs from Git Bash with its stdout and exit code intact.

Sources:
- Command line tutorial: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html
- gdUnit4 command line tool: https://godot-gdunit-labs.github.io/gdUnit4/latest/advanced_testing/cmd/
- gdUnit4 releases: https://github.com/godot-gdunit-labs/gdUnit4/releases
- Godot 4.7 migration guide: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html
- Godot 4.7 release notes: https://godotengine.org/releases/4.7/
- GDScript reference, lambda functions and rest parameters: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html

## Platform (4.5+)

- **visionOS export**: First new platform since open-sourcing (windowed app mode)
- **SDL3 gamepad driver**: Better cross-platform gamepad support
- **Android**: Edge-to-edge display, camera feed access, 16KB page support (Android 15+)
- **Linux**: Wayland subwindow support for multi-window capability

This is TR-section-028 and the first half of TR-section-013.

139	**Source layout (ADR-0010).** `src/sim/layout/`: `layout_module.gd` (owner, registration, callables), `layout_state.gd`, `layout_derived.gd`, `layout_ids.gd`, `socket_ref.gd`, `layout_faults.gd`, `layout_mutators.gd` (LM1 to LM4 and checks), `weld_math.gd` and `detach_planner.gd` (pure), `door_leaves.gd` (the hook), `layout_restore.gd` (validation), `views/` (`LayoutViews` and the record classes of § 11), `ports/layout_graph_port.gd` (`@abstract`, § 8). The PROJECTOR is `src/presentation/projector/` and is never imported from here. The pure compile of authored runs into the rect table (`TemplateCompiler`) lives under `src/data/sections/` beside the loader that calls it, owned by Layout by review, not by import (ADR-0007 § 1.9).

141	### 2. The snapshot payload: dense parallel columns, ascending ids, tombstones kept
142	
143	`snapshot(ctx)` calls `ctx.put(payload)` with a `Dictionary` whose keys are `String`s. Every table is a set of **parallel columns** (TR-section-006): no `Dictionary` is keyed by an id, no `Vector2i`/`Rect2i`/`Color`/`Resource`/`StringName`, no `PackedStringArray`, and every packed array in the payload is a `duplicate()` (ADR-0003 snapshot contract; registry `live_reference_in_snapshot_payload`). The key set is closed; the AC-130 allow-list file is regenerated from this table.
144	
145	| Payload key | Type | Contents (row order) |
146	|---|---|---|
147	| `schema_version` | `int` | `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SCHEMA_VERSION` |
148	| `counters` | `Dictionary` of three `int`s | `next_section_id`, `next_body_id`, `next_room_id` (first allocated id is 1, so `default_state` sets all three to 1) |
149	| `bodies` | `Dictionary` | `body_id` (`PackedInt32Array`), `origin_section_id` (`PackedInt32Array`), `state` (`PackedByteArray`: 0 `LIVE`, 1 `DISSOLVED`); ascending `body_id` |
150	| `instances` | `Dictionary` of 14 columns | `section_id`, `body_id`, `offset_x`, `offset_y`, `room_id_base`, `node_base`, `edge_base`, `comp_base`, `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash`, `structure_hash` (all `PackedInt32Array`); `rot_q`, `discarded` (`PackedByteArray`); `template_id` (`Array[String]`); ascending `section_id` |
151	| `sockets` | `Dictionary` | `section_id` (`PackedInt32Array`), `socket_index` (`PackedByteArray`), `state` (`PackedByteArray`: 1 `WELDED`, 2 `CAPPED`, 3 `CUT_OPEN`; `FREE` = 0 is never stored), `seam_id` (`PackedInt32Array`); ascending `(section_id, socket_index)`; only non-`FREE` sockets have a row |
152	| `welds` | `Dictionary` | `seam_id`, `section_a`, `section_b` (`PackedInt32Array`), `socket_a`, `socket_b`, `state` (`PackedByteArray`; `state`: 0 `ACTIVE`, 1 `CUT_SEALED`, 2 `CUT_RAGGED`), `welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T` (`PackedInt64Array`); ascending `seam_id` |

154	Decisions inside the shape:
155	
156	- **Ids are dense ordinals: `section_id == row + 1` and `body_id == row + 1`.** A section or body id is consumed only by the mutator that appends its row, in the same call, so no id exists without a row. Row lookup is then an index, not a map: no `Dictionary` on the read path, no `bsearch` for the common query. Restore verifies the equality (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_COUNTER`). The cost is that a future "reserve an id then maybe not use it" idea is forbidden by this ADR, which is the right pressure (§ Risks R1).
157	- **`template_id` is a typed `Array[String]` column** (TR-section-004). The alternatives were the ledger integer (rejected: the GDD allow-list, LY-6 b and every restore reason name the string; four templates; saves are disposable pre-release; a human-readable dump matters more than 4 bytes a row) and a `PackedStringArray` (rejected: not on ADR-0006's allow-list). **Probed 2026-10-29:** a typed `Array[String]` survives `var_to_bytes`/`bytes_to_var` still typed.
158	- **64-bit times are native `PackedInt64Array` columns** (TR-section-006). ADR-0006 § 1.2 item 3 allows full-width `int` and § 1.3 limits the halves convention to values that can reach JSON; `welded_at_T`/`cut_at_T` reach JSON only through the dev `dump-save`, which renders any `int` of magnitude 2^53 or more as a decimal string and `T` is bounded below 2^53. The GDD's two-halves form stays legal and is not used.
159	- **The three hashes are stored as signed int32 and compared as `value & 0xFFFFFFFF`** (`IntMath.low32`, ADR-0005 P9; probed 2026-10-29). A comparison without the mask is a lint-visible defect (AC-172 c).
160	- **`rot_q` is a byte column that must be 0.** It is stored so the field exists in schema v1 and a later rotation feature is not a layout change; any nonzero value is `LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED` at restore and a boot error in a template that asks for it.
161	- **`socket_index` is the template's declaration ordinal** of that socket, a `uint8` (MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION never exceeds 8 and is lint-bounded by `MAX_SEAMS_PER_SECTION`). A runtime socket handle is the packed int `SocketRef = (section_id << 4) | socket_index` (`socket_ref.gd`, 24 bits at the section-id ceiling), used as an argument, a memo key and a sort key; it is never persisted.
162	- **Seam ids are the Graph's.** A `welds` row's `seam_id` is whatever `weld_join` returned; Layout allocates none and treats it as an opaque positive `int32`. After a cut the two sockets keep their `seam_id` (state `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN`) because the scar's bead and cap plate are drawn from that history (Pillar 5).
163	- **The payload size rule holds.** The largest realistic shape (D.21's long campaign) is tens of KB, far under `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES`; `snapshot()` computes the D.21 estimate from row counts and raises the one-shot diagnostic `layout_block_soft_bytes` when it exceeds `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SOFT_BYTES` (GDD Tuning Knobs); the hard ceiling is Save/Load's (TR-section-030).
164	
165	**Tombstones.** A discarded section keeps its row with `discarded = 1` and its `body_id`; the body it sat on becomes `DISSOLVED`; its `socket` and `welds` rows stay (a surviving mate keeps its `CAPPED`/`CUT_OPEN` history). Ids stay consumed, so nothing is ever reused or renumbered (TR-section-005).

167	### 3. ID allocation and the split with the Graph (ADR-LAY-05)
168	
169	| Id | Allocator | Counter and home | Range and rule |
170	|---|---|---|---|
171	| `section_id` | **Layout** | `next_section_id` in `layout.state` | first 1; `<= 2^20 - 1` so `rect_key` fits 32 bits (D.9); `can_build` returns `CAPACITY` before consuming `2^20` |
172	| `body_id` | **Layout** | `next_body_id` in `layout.state` | first 1; `<= 2^31 - 1` (int32 column); one new id per LM1 and per LM3 |
173	| `room_id` | **Layout** | `next_room_id` in `layout.state` | first 1; `<= 2^31 - 1`; **contiguous per instance**: `room_id = room_id_base + room_index`, `room_index` the room's declaration order in the template |
174	| `node_id`, `edge_id`, `compartment_id` | **Graph** | `next_node_id`, `next_edge_id`, comp counter in `graph.state` | returned by M1 as `{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}` and stored by Layout per instance as `graph_ref_base` |
175	| `seam_id`, opening ids | **Graph** | `next_seam_id` in `graph.state` | given to Layout in LM2's arguments and read back through `seam_view` |
176	| `section_id` in `graph.state` | follows Layout | `next_section_id` in `graph.state` | M1 advances it to `max(section_id) + 1`; Layout never reads it except in the post-restore verification |
177	
178	**Mapping rules (all derived, none persisted).**
179	
180	- Template-local index to Graph id: `node_id = node_base + node_ref_index`, `edge_id = edge_base + edge_ref_index`; template-local room to compartment: `comp_id = comp_base + room_index`; room to id: `room_id = room_id_base + room_index`. Hence `compartment_of_room(room_id) = comp_base(section) + (room_id - room_id_base(section))` and the inverse.
181	- Reverse lookup (a Graph id or a `room_id` to its section) is a `bsearch` over the ascending base column (`node_base`, `edge_base`, `comp_base`, `room_id_base` are all ascending because every allocator is monotone and rows append). A section whose range does not contain the id answers `NONE` (a discarded section's `anchor_geometry` answers nothing, without an error, FT:703).
182	- These rules require the Graph to return **contiguous** node, edge and compartment ranges **in template order** from M1 (cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011) and to size each range from the template alone, so the post-restore check "node, edge and compartment counts match the template" is a pure comparison.
183	
184	**When ids are consumed.** LM1 reads (does not yet advance) `next_section_id`, `next_body_id` and `next_room_id`, calls the Graph's M1 with the section id, and only on an `OK` status appends the rows and advances the counters. So a Graph defect leaves Layout's counters and tables untouched (fail-closed per ADR-0003 § 5; the kernel is `FAULTED` anyway). `can_build` and `can_detach` test every counter ceiling **before** any id is consumed or the Graph is called, so no counter ever wraps (TR-section-037).
185	
186	**Why Layout owns the section id.** The Graph's M1 takes "a caller section id" (LS-15, LS-19), the Graph's `next_section_id` then follows Layout's, and Layout needs the section id to exist before the Graph does (it keys the dirty key and the body row). The alternative of the Graph allocating it (§ Alternatives 4) would make Layout's `build_section` depend on a return value to name its own row and would put the `rect_key` bound (2^20) in the Graph's hands.
187	
188	### 4. Template identity, the ledger nesting (OQ-B) and the three hashes (ADR-LAY-04, -06)
189	
190	**Ledger nesting (ADR-0007 OQ-B).** `assets/data/sections/ids.lock.json` is one `section_templates` space with one flat `pairs[]`, exactly the shape ADR-0007 § 3.2 defines, so `LedgerCheck.verify` stays generic and the append-only CI gate needs no second format. Two classes share the space, told apart by **key shape**: a template pair has key `<template_id>`, a room pair has key `<template_id>/<room_key>` (the `/` is illegal inside a snake_case key, so the split is unambiguous). Template ids come from the low part of the declared range and room ids from above a fixed boundary (a `SectionLedgerCheck` in `src/data/sections/`, owned by Layout by review, checks the boundary, that every room pair's prefix is a template pair in the same ledger, and that retiring or dormanting a template does the same to its room pairs: lint `LEDGER_ROOM_ORPHAN`). One entry per `room_key` rather than a nested list keeps `dormant` and `retired_ids` per room, so removing one room from a template is a per-pair `dormant` flip and a renamed room is a visible new pair, which is the diff a migration step needs. The integers are **not persisted in `layout.state`** (the instance persists the `template_id` string, § 2); they exist so a rename or removal after `SHIPPED` is detected and migrated (ADR-0007 § 3.3), and so later blocks can reference a room by integer if they must.
191	
192	**The three hashes (the shape of ADR-LAY-06).** ADR-0005 § 3.1 forbids an owner-written `[u32 tag][u32 length][payload]` byte string, and § 4.6 already defines the template hashes as `Hash64.of_value` of a post-cast sub-payload "whose shape is Layout's and ADR-0013's". So ADR-LAY-06 becomes the **`Dictionary` shape of three sub-payloads**, hashed once by `SectionTemplates` at catalog freeze and stored as `low32` in the template row (never in the template file, ADR-0007 § 3.5):
193	
194	| Hash | Payload (keys sorted by the encoder, so order in source is irrelevant; every family is one flat `PackedInt32Array` in the field order of its LY-4 row, strings replaced by template-local indices, variable-length members as a CSR `*_off` array plus a data array) | Changes when |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| `geometry_hash` | `size_tiles`; `rooms` (origin, flags, tile runs); `wall_runs` (orientation, start, length, kind, flanking rooms, `face_h_px`, `face_variant`); the compiled `rects` (stride 7: `x0, y0, x1, y1, flags, owner_kind, owner_ref`, in `idx` order, leaf and variant slots at their closed or full extent); `doors`; `sockets` with their `lanes`; `hardpoints`; `plate_positions`; `loose_slots`; `story_slots`; `anchors` (polyline CSR); `fixture_anchors`; `instrument_placements` (geometry fields only) | anything that decides where a rectangle, tile, socket, door or anchor is |
197	| `visual_hash` | `dialect`; kit-piece ids and layers; art references; labels; advisory hints (`socket_tag`); flags no query reads | only presentation changes |
198	| `structure_hash` | the **ordered** key sequences: `room_key[]`, `socket_key[]`, `door_key[]`, `hp_key[]`, `node_ref[]`, `edge_ref[]`, `anchor_key[]`, `slot_id[]`; each room's sorted tile list | any reorder, add, remove or rename of an identity-bearing element, or any tile-set change |
199	
200	**Why a third hash.** LY-26 e classifies a template change as "structural" when the *sets* of keys or a room's tile set differ, but the block persists only two hashes, so the check has nothing to compare against except Graph counts. A pure **reordering** (rooms `[a, b]` to `[b, a]`) keeps every set equal and every count equal, yet `room_id = room_id_base + room_index`, `socket_index` and `comp_base + room_index` all index the *current* template by position, so an existing save would silently attach its Graph compartments and welded sockets to the wrong rooms and sockets. LY-6 e's sentence "a template that merely reorders rooms changes ids only for NEW instances" is therefore wrong as written. The remedy is to persist what the check needs: `structure_hash` is one more `int32` per instance (§ 2), costs four bytes a row, and makes the structural rule exact: **a `structure_hash` mismatch is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` for every instance, history or not**, because every instance has Graph data built from the old order. `geometry_hash` keeps the GDD's history-dependent rule (§ 10). The third hash is not redundant with `geometry_hash`: because `rooms` are encoded in declaration order, a reorder already changes `geometry_hash`, which on an instance **with history** is refused by the GDD's own rule; the marginal value of `structure_hash` is the **never-welded `FREE` instance**, where the history-dependent rule would accept the change as `geometry_changed_fresh` and silently re-point `room_id_base + room_index`, `comp_base + room_index` and `socket_index` to the wrong rooms and sockets. This is a deliberate deviation from the TR text "13-int section-instance rows" (the row is 14 columns, one of them the string); it is listed first among the decisions for the user's review.
201	
202	**Two more template rules.** (a) Every coordinate of a footprint rectangle, socket `line_px`/`start_px`, room `origin_px` and wall run lies on the 24-px grid (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`) except a door leaf's moving edge (LY-3 a, LY-7); `GRID_24` is a **BOOT invariant** (`CONTENT_INVARIANT`, ADR-0007 § 2.4), not only a CI lint, because the closure of the weld offset on the grid (§ 7) and the broadphase cell alignment depend on it; a 12-px shift in a socket fails the load (TR-derelict-033 Layout half). (b) `area_max <= 0` on a door is the one named structural invariant D.5 needs (it divides by it) and refuses the load; the published `area_max` range is guidance (ADR-0007 § 2.5).
203	
204	### 5. Rectangles, units and frames: the record, the flags and the reserved `idx` space
205	
206	ADR-0014 owns the broadphase, `QueryBuffer`, `OccluderSource` and the query signatures. This ADR owns **what a rectangle is, how it is keyed and which ones can exist**.
207	
208	- **The record (TR-section-010).** A rect is `(x0, y0, x1, y1)` in section-local base px, **half-open** `[x0, x1) x [y0, y1)` over pixel cells, with one flags byte: `SOLID`, `OCCLUDES_LIGHT`, `DOOR_LEAF`, `PROP`, `MACHINE`, `HULL` (registry `layout_rect_flags`). The legal flag combinations are LY-7's table and a boot error otherwise (`RECT_FLAGS_ILLEGAL`). A rect with `x1 <= x0` or `y1 <= y0` is omitted from every result but keeps its `idx`.
209	- **Units and frames.** The unit is the base pixel; `TILE_PX` is the floor tile and `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` the wall depth. There is no world frame in Layout. Reads answer **section-local** except those that answer for one body (`rects_in`, `solid_in`, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `section_at`, `weld_offset`, `detach_preview`), which answer in the **body frame** = section-local + `offset_px(section_id)` (LY-3 c).
210	- **Transforms are integer translation only.** No rotation, no mirror, no zoom value appears anywhere in Layout (LY-3 d, e). Every px-to-tile or px-to-cell conversion is **floor** division through `IntMath.floor_div` (body-frame coordinates may be negative after a detach re-base); the bare `/` and `%` operators appear nowhere in `src/sim/layout/` (ADR-0010 `SIM-05`).
211	- **The `idx` space is compiled once per template and never changes** (D.9): static rects sorted by `(y0, x0, y1, x1, flags)` are `0 .. N_static - 1`; one reserved leaf slot per door follows in door declaration order; two reserved variant slots (PLATE, JAMB) per **hatched** socket follow, `idx = N_static + N_doors + 2h + v`. The key `(section_id, idx)` is therefore stable across attach, detach, restore and animation: a state change only switches slots between active and inactive; an inactive or zero-length slot is omitted from results and keeps its `idx` (TR-section-020's "renumbers nothing" half).
212	- **Rect keys.** `rect_key = section_id * RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` with the stride `MAX_RECTS_PER_SECTION` (GDD Tuning Knobs, a power of two) and `idx < stride`; the key reaches `2^32 - 1`, so every key column is `PackedInt64Array` (ADR-0014 owns the buffer). Boot refuses a template whose `N_static + N_doors + 2 N_hatched` exceeds the stride (`RECT_STRIDE_OVERFLOW`).
213	- **The compiled table is catalog data.** `SectionTemplate` exposes rect `idx`-indexed accessors (`rect_count()`, `rect_x0(i)`, `rect_y0(i)`, `rect_x1(i)`, `rect_y1(i)`, `rect_flags(i)`, `rect_owner_kind(i)`, `rect_owner_ref(i)`), never a packed array (ADR-0007 § 1.5). The bulk read that builds a body's grid at build, attach, detach and restore is ADR-0014's; those events are cold, so accessor calls are acceptable there (V3 measures them).
214	- **Static footprint set versus query set.** `rects_in` returns `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rects and `solid_in` returns `SOLID` rects in their *current leaf state*; the mating overlap test of § 6 uses the **static** set with all flags, so a door animating can never flip a verdict. Both sets are views of one rect set (Pillar 1: collision, light and drawing cannot disagree); neither is an engine collision shape, and the avatar has no physics body.
215	
216	### 6. Sockets, seams and the mating predicate
217	
218	- **A socket is a pre-declared attachment site** `{socket_key, facing N|E|S|W, line_px, start_px, width_tiles, class_id, lanes[], hatch | none}` in the template (LY-13). `pos_px` is `(line_px, start_px)` for E/W facings and `(start_px, line_px)` for N/S. The four-facing footprint, LOW-end, PLATE/JAMB/LEAF table of LY-13 is normative and is not restated.
219	- **States (TR-section-018, TR-assembly-025).** `FREE -> WELDED(seam_id) -> CAPPED` (after a SEALED cut) or `CUT_OPEN` (after a RAGGED cut); `CAPPED` and `CUT_OPEN` never return to `FREE` in MVP, which supports exactly one weld-then-cut cycle per socket. **A socket's state is written only inside LM2 and LM3.** There is no `install_cap_plate`, no `set_socket_state` and no setter on `LayoutState.sockets`; `socket_state` writes are private to `weld_math`/`detach_planner` helpers called by those two mutators, and a lint (`LAY-SOCKET-01`, tier E1, ADR-0010 § 6) rejects any other write to the `sockets` columns.
220	- **`can_attach` is a pure, first-failure-wins reason chain** (TR-section-019), cheap before expensive, in this fixed order: `SOCKET_UNKNOWN`, `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, `SAME_BODY`, `FACING_MISMATCH`, `WIDTH_MISMATCH`, `CLASS_MISMATCH`, `LANE_MISMATCH`, `GEOM_OVERLAP`. `SAME_BODY` being a hard reject and every weld merging two bodies is what makes the weld relation a **forest** and a cut always split a body into exactly two components.
221	- **`GEOM_OVERLAP`.** The test set is the static footprint of both bodies after the D.6 translation: every static rect with all flags, each PLATE slot at its full footprint, no leaf and no JAMB slot, plus the tile cells of every room (rect against tile and tile against tile, so a wall over the other body's floor and two floors on one cell both fail); abutting is legal. It runs over each body's broadphase handle (ADR-0014) and is **memoised on `(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, static_version_a, static_version_b)`**; uncached cost target <= 2 ms (TR-section-019), a pending-spike figure (V3). The memo is a small fixed-capacity ring in `LayoutDerived`, reset on restore.
222	- **Slot activation is a pure function** of `(this socket's state, this socket's hatch, the mate's hatch, W)` evaluated by LM1 to LM4 and `post_restore` (the LY-15 matrix); no persisted field is needed because the mate's hatch is known from the two templates. A hatched socket whose mate is bare is `hatch_one_sided`: legal, behaves bulkhead-only, its PLATE stays on while `WELDED`.
223	- **The `can_attach` preview needs more than a reason**, and a Class A check returns a bare `StringName` (ADR-0003 § 5). So the payload `{reason, hatch_one_sided, openings_count}` is its own pure read, `preview_attach(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, out: AttachPreview) -> void`, and `can_attach(...)` is `preview_attach` followed by returning `out.reason` (`&""` = OK). One implementation, two shapes.
224	- **`socket_plan(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, out: WeldPlan)`** is a pure read that fills the Graph's weld-plan DATA verbatim (one lane pair per lane in `(loop, lane_index)` order, one opening per mated hatch pair `(comp_a, comp_b, area_max)`, `L_seam = width_tiles`). The field layout of `WeldPlan` follows ADR-0011's `JoinPlan`; Layout fills it, Assembly adds `q`, the Graph's `can_join` validates, and both verdicts must pass before apply.
225	
226	### 7. Weld offsets, bodies and the detach re-base
227	
228	**Bodies.** `bodies[]` is Layout's: `{body_id, origin_section_id, state}`. **Every built section starts on its own new body at offset (0, 0), and every multi-section body is produced by welds only** (LY-25): there is no "place on an existing body" path, so the forest property holds by construction. A body's frame origin is the origin of its `origin_section_id`.
229	
230	**Weld offset (D.6, TR-section-021).** `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b`, where `a` is the **survivor-side** socket and `b` the absorbed-side socket, assigned **by body, never by argument order**: the body with the **lower `body_id`** survives (the older body; the home ship in the MVP). `attach_section` re-labels the two arguments internally, so `attach_section(x, y, ...)` and `attach_section(y, x, ...)` produce the same survivor, the same `offset_b`, the same `frame_shift_px`, and a **byte-identical** `layout.state`: the `welds[]` row always records the survivor-side section and socket as `section_a`/`socket_a` (canonicalisation). `weld_math.gd` is a pure module of integer helpers (`survivor_of`, `offset_b`, `frame_shift`) with no state, which `weld_offset(...)` (the pure read), `can_attach` and LM2 all call, so prediction and apply cannot drift.
231	
232	**24-grid closure.** `pos_a`, `pos_b` and `offset_a` lie on the 24-px grid (`GRID_24` is a boot invariant, § 4), and `offset_a` does by induction from (0, 0), so `offset_b` does; an off-grid `offset_b` from a validated plan is therefore a **defect**, not a reason code: `apply` raises `LAYOUT_OFFSET_OFF_GRID` (domain 4) and returns its negative.
233	
234	**LM2 effects, in order** (all inside the caller's single P2 apply, after the Graph's `weld_join`): append the `welds[]` row (`ACTIVE`); upsert both socket rows to `WELDED(seam_id)` keeping ascending order; shift every section of the absorbed body by `frame_shift_px = offset_b - offset_b_old` and move it to the survivor `body_id`; mark the absorbed body `DISSOLVED`; switch the PLATE/JAMB/LEAF slots of both sockets (§ 6); seed each newly active LEAF **closed** with its last-projected cache (§ 8); rebuild the affected broadphase handles (ADR-0014); bump `static_version` and `version` of **every section whose socket state changed (including the host section that does not move) and every moved section**; stamp `changed_region` (REGION for the two socket-host sections, FRAME for the other moved sections); cache the mated hatch's opening ids from `seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]` into `opening_leaves`; mark `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<survivor>`, `BODY/<absorbed>` and `SEC/<id>` for each affected section (5 keys for the MVP weld of two single-section bodies). The returned `AttachResult` carries `{surviving_body_id, absorbed_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px}`; `body_of` of every moved section is the survivor in the same apply and is readable by any ordered reader in the same tick.
235	
236	**LM3 and the detach re-base (D.12).** After the Graph's `cut_detach`, LM3 marks the weld row `CUT_SEALED` or `CUT_RAGGED` with `cut_at_T`; sets both sockets `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN` (keeping `seam_id`); then **enumerates the connected components of the `ACTIVE` weld forest minus the cut seam, in ascending `section_id`**. The component containing the body's `origin_section_id` keeps its `body_id`; the other receives a new `body_id` from `next_body_id`, its `origin_section_id` is `m`, the minimum `section_id` of that component, and its offsets are re-based by `frame_shift = offset_old(m)` (`offset_new(s) = offset_old(s) - frame_shift`). The traversal uses preallocated `PackedInt32Array` stack and visited columns in `LayoutDerived`, bounded by `MAX_SECTIONS`, so no container is built in the apply. `DetachPlanner.plan(...)` is the single implementation behind both `detach_preview(seam_id)` and LM3, so the preview and the apply cannot drift (Assembly's `MSA_SHIFT_DRIFT`). A cut that does not yield exactly two components is a defect (`LAYOUT_COMPONENT_COUNT`), unreachable by the forest argument. The `DetachResult` is `{new_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px, rects[]}` with `rects[]` the cut seam's two hatch rectangles in the pre-cut body frame, **computed before the sockets change**, exactly equal to `detach_preview(seam_id).rects`. Layout performs **no actor check** (it reads nothing from `body.state`): the CHANNEL path is vetoed by Assembly's completion validate, and Body's `rebase_on_detach` is the net behind it (LY-17, BDY-24 iii).
237	
238	**Why not argument order or "the larger body".** Argument order makes the dissolved body depend on a caller's mixup (the home ship could dissolve) and makes the block bytes differ between two equal worlds, which breaks AC-172 (equal blocks by different histories hash equal). "Larger body survives" would make survival depend on a count that changes with every weld. The lower `body_id` is a persisted, immutable, total order.
239	
240	### 8. The door leaf, the `layout.doors` hook and the Graph port
241	
242	**One rectangle per leaf.** A door or hatch has one leaf rect. With `width_px` (the 96-px door cell), the Graph opening's `area` clamped to `[0, area_max]` and `area_max > 0`: `gap = floor_div(width_px * area, area_max)`, `leaf_w = width_px - gap`, and the rect is anchored to the hinge side with depth `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` (D.5; hinge LOW for every socket hatch so both leaves of a mated hatch retract the same way). `leaf_w = 0` returns no rect and keeps its `idx`. A mated hatch is two leaves (one per section) driven by one `area`.
243	
244	**The port.** Layout reads and calls the Graph only through `LayoutGraphPort` (`src/sim/layout/ports/layout_graph_port.gd`, `@abstract`, ADR-0010 § 3), implemented by the Graph's facade and injected into `setup()`:
245	
246	```gdscript
247	@abstract class_name LayoutGraphPort extends RefCounted
248	@abstract func check_instantiate(views: SimViews, template_id: String) -> StringName   # Graph CAPACITY pre-check for can_build
249	@abstract func instantiate_section(scope: WriteScope, section_id: int, template_id: String, kind: int, out: SectionBases) -> int
250	@abstract func opening_into(edge_id: int, out: OpeningRead) -> bool   # false = unknown edge; fills area, area_max, door_state
251	@abstract func seam_openings_into(seam_id: int, out: SeamOpenings) -> bool   # opening_ids[] in socket_plan.openings order
252	@abstract func section_counts_into(section_id: int, out: SectionCounts) -> bool   # nodes, edges, compartments, next_section_id (verification only)
253	```
254	
255	The 4.7 typed-return rule applies to any override of a typed-return abstract method, so each implementation returns explicitly on every path (a stub that omits a return is a parse error or a defect found by V-lint). The reads are allocation-free (caller-owned `out`), valid in P3 and in P2 after the Graph's own writes.

256	
257	**The hook (TR-section-012).** `layout.doors`: `hook_id &"layout.doors"`, owner Layout, `divisor 1`, `offset 0`, `after []`, running in P3. Body's `body.integrate` is registered `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]` (BDY-8), which orders the Emitter after it transitively, so every P3 reader sees same-tick leaves. The hook loops over the `LayoutDerived` leaf cache, a dense list of at most `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` slots in ascending `(section_id, door_index)` (deterministic bump order):
258	
259	1. `graph.opening_into(edge, op)`. If it returns false (unknown opening) the leaf stays at its last projected value (closed at the template default), `area` is never invented, `leaf_version` is not bumped, and the diagnostic `opening_unknown` is raised **once per edge** (a bit in the slot's flags, cleared when the read succeeds again) (TR-section-035). A `area_max <= 0` read is treated the same way and counted `opening_invalid`.
260	2. `area` is clamped to `[0, area_max]`; a value above `area_max` raises the diagnostic `area_clamped` and uses `area_max` (TR-section-035).
261	3. `leaf_w` is computed (integer, `IntMath.floor_div`), compared with the slot's last-projected value, and if different the leaf rect is recomputed and the slot's section is flagged.
262	4. After the loop, for each flagged section in ascending id: `leaf_version += 1`, `version += 1`, never `static_version`; `changed_region` is stamped REGION(union of the old and new leaf rectangles). **At most one bump per section per tick** (TR-section-042).
263	5. If any section was flagged, the hook opens `layout.state` once (`scope.open_for`) and marks one **`LEAF/<section_id>`** key per flagged section.
264	
265	**Why the hook marks a key, and why a new kind.** `layout.doors` changes only derived caches, yet the PROJECTOR must redraw a leaf whose rect changed and the door leaf sprite extent must equal the leaf rect with no tween (TR-section-013). ADR-0009 presenters draw from dirty batches; polling every section's counter every frame would add a read per frame for an event that happens a few times per play. Marking is legal (ADR-0004 § 7: a key marked for an unchanged value is not a violation; the HOOK scope may open any block). Its cost is that a granted `open_for` advances `touch_serial`, invalidating the block hash cache (ADR-0005 § 5.2) on those ticks; under the binary door model that is a few ticks per play, and the re-encode is bounded by the block size (tens of KB). LY-32's closed list is SEC, BODY, SEAM; a leaf change under `SEC/<id>` would also wake Failure & Trail's anchor rebuild and Lighting's static rebuild on every door toggle, so the key family **`LEAF` (kind 4)** is added to Layout's own key space (ADR-0004 § 3 leaves unnumbered families to the owner). Subscribers that care (the PROJECTOR, Lighting's dynamic leaf patch) test `batch.has(key)`; the rest ignore it.
266	
267	**The correctness condition.** Every `area` write of a template door or mated hatch lands in **P2** by command (a SYSTEM-origin `set_opening` re-submitted each tick by Interaction's `attempts[]` for a `CLOSING_BLOCKED` retry); no Graph phase writes `area` or `door_state` of such an opening (the Graph's virtual breach and seam-weep openings have no leaf and are neither read nor projected). Layout stores, mirrors and writes neither value (TR-section-013); `layout_hash` does not cover door state. This is a cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0011/0012/0020 and a test (AC "closed leaf blocks and an open one does not in the same tick its state changes").
268	
269	**Seeding.** LM1 reads the just-created openings through the port and derives each leaf immediately (the Graph holds authored initial areas), so there is no tick in which a built door is wrong. **LM2 does not read the Graph's `area`:** it initialises each newly active LEAF **closed** (`leaf_w = width_px`) and seeds the last-projected cache with that value in the same apply, because `weld_join` starts the new opening at `area` 0; reads between the P2 apply and the first P3 hook therefore see a solid span, raise no `stale_leaf`, and the hook bumps `leaf_version` only if its `area` read differs (TR-section-034). `post_restore` derives all leaves in one `derive_doors` pass (§ 10).
270	
271	**Pure leaf queries.** `leaf_would_overlap(opening_edge_id, area, boxes: PackedInt32Array) -> bool` and `leaf_obstruction_into(opening_edge_id, area, boxes, out: LeafObstruction) -> bool` evaluate **every** leaf projected from that opening (`opening_leaves`: both sections of a mated hatch) at the new `area`, in the body frame, against every caller-supplied foot box (`boxes` is a flat half-open `x0, y0, x1, y1` array the caller owns); Layout reads nothing from `body.state` (TR-section-014). `door_passage_into(section_id, via_id, out: DoorPassage) -> bool` returns `{orientation, sill_rect, gap_rect, open_extent_px}` from the leaf value `layout.doors` last projected (so collision, light and passage cannot disagree and `opening` is not re-read); an unknown or discarded section or `via_id` returns false with no error; before `post_restore` it reports `open_extent_px` 0 and raises `stale_leaf`. The single passability rule is a pure helper `DoorPassage.passable(open_extent_px, orientation, foot_extent_ew, foot_extent_ns)`: passable iff `open_extent_px` is at least the foot extent across the doorway (the Body foot box, BDY-14: 16 across an east-west run, 8 across a north-south run, supplied by Body as constants, not owned here) (TR-horror-032).
272	
273	**Cost.** The hook is an integer multiply and divide per door plus one port call and compare. Target <= 0.2 ms at `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` animating doors (5 percent of `STEP_BUDGET_MS`) on a release export, a pending-spike figure (V2). The fallback ladder is ADR-0010 § 9: cache accessors in locals, then early-out on an unchanged Graph `touch` counter if ADR-0011 publishes one, before any native rung.
274	
275	### 9. Mutators, checks, results, faults and dirty keys
276	
277	Layout has **exactly four mutators, all Class A**, and no Class B (it holds no quantity that can sensibly be clamped) (TR-section-020). Each has a pure check; `apply` is infallible once its check passed and a failure inside it is a defect that returns `-fault_code` after `scope.fault`.
278

314	### 10. Restore, drift and `post_restore`
315	
316	**`restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` is two-phase** (ADR-0003 § 2, ADR-0006 § 2.2): decode and validate into a `LayoutScratch` (cold path, allocation allowed); on any failure call `ctx.fault(code, detail)` and write nothing; on success **copy the contents into the existing `LayoutState` object** (each column assigned from the scratch's own arrays, none aliasing `data`), then rebuild the static `LayoutDerived` (lookups, socket index, caps, version counters reset to 1, `mutation_count` 0, memo cleared, broadphase handles rebuilt by ADR-0014's call). A restore swaps whole tables only on success (TR-section-007).
317	
318	**Validation, in order** (first failure wins, with a named detail): (1) `stored_version` in `supported_versions` and the key set equals the § 2 table, every column has the declared type and equal row counts per table (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_SCHEMA`); (2) every `template_id` resolves in the catalog (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE`); (3) `rot_q` all 0 (`LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED`); (4) the drift policy below (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED`); (5) dense ids: `section_id[i] == i + 1`, `body_id[i] == i + 1`, `room_id_base[i + 1] == room_id_base[i] + rooms(template[i])`, counters equal the dense count + 1 and below the ceilings (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_COUNTER`); (6) references: every non-discarded instance sits on a `LIVE` body, every `LIVE` body has an in-range `origin_section_id` that belongs to it, socket rows are strictly ascending with `socket_index < template.socket_count` and a resolving `seam_id`, weld rows ascend and agree with their socket states (`ACTIVE` with two `WELDED`, `CUT_SEALED` with two `CAPPED`, `CUT_RAGGED` with two `CUT_OPEN`), `ACTIVE` welds form a forest whose components are exactly the `LIVE` bodies' section sets, and every `ACTIVE` weld's offsets satisfy `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b` on the 24 grid (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING`). An unsupported `stored_version` is a reported failure, never a silent default.
319	
320	**Drift policy (TR-section-007).** The current template's three hashes are compared with the stored ones after `& 0xFFFFFFFF`. A **`structure_hash`** difference is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` for every instance (§ 4). A **`geometry_hash`** difference is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` when the instance carries history, meaning any non-`FREE` socket, any `welds[]` row naming it, or a body shared with another section, because a moved socket or wall edge under a welded or cut instance restores with broken abutment; on a never-welded `FREE` instance alone it is accepted with the diagnostic `geometry_changed_fresh`, the rects are re-derived from the new template and the stored hash is rewritten. A **`visual_hash`** difference alone is accepted with `visual_changed` and rewritten. A hash collision cannot hide a structural change that also changes a tile set or key sequence in a way the validation of step (6) detects; a 2^-32 collision on `structure_hash` is accepted and recorded (§ Risks R6). Pre-release saves are disposable; after the first outside build the migration obligation of LY-6 e applies, and a rewritten hash means the next snapshot differs from the stored one, so the K-4 `state_hash` compare reports a mismatch as a diagnostic, as designed.
321	
322	**Query validity after restore.** Class 1 (static, valid when `restore()` returns): `room_at`, `V`, `exposed_tiles`, `room_surface`, `socket_plan`, `anchor_geometry`, static rect membership, `section_offset`, `body_of`, `section_at`. Class 2 (leaf-dependent, valid after `post_restore()`): `rects_in`/`solid_in` door leaves, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `door_passage_into`. Between the two they report the template default (every leaf closed) and raise `stale_leaf` if read; `LayoutDerived.leaves_valid` is the flag. The kernel guarantees every `restore()` completes before any `post_restore()` begins.
323	
324	**`post_restore(ctx)`** (a) runs one `derive_doors` pass over the leaf cache using `opening_into` (an `area` above `area_max` is clamped with a diagnostic, and the same fault found *here* is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_DANGLING`; an unknown opening leaves the leaf closed); (b) rebuilds `opening_leaves` from the restored `welds[]` and `seam_openings_into`; (c) bumps `version` and `leaf_version` (never `static_version`) for each section whose derived leaf set differs from the all-closed default, so a restored open door is a 1 to 2 transition and every rebuilding consumer rebuilds on tick 1 with no ordering between `post_restore` calls; (d) runs cross-block **verification** through `section_counts_into`: every `graph_ref_base` resolves (node, edge and compartment counts match the template), every `welds[]` `seam_id` resolves to a Graph seam record, and `graph.next_section_id == layout.next_section_id`. Failures use the restore codes. Verification order and the "installed `def_id` at a hardpoint resolves" diagnostic belong to ADR-0016's verifier list; this ADR supplies the checks Layout's side can run. After a restore every section reports `changed_region` ALL once, and the kernel delivers one `ALL` batch (ADR-0003 § 4).
325	
326	**Policy line (TR-derelict-008 Layout half).** A save restores from its **saved values**: templates are never mutated at runtime, a restore never re-templates an instance, and no Authoring content lint runs at restore.

328	### 11. Read views: records, tiers, order and frames
329	
330	Reads are pure, side-effect free, deterministic and identical before a snapshot and after restoring it (idempotent), and have **no "perceived" variant** (Pillar 1, TR-section-039). They are exposed through the long-lived `LayoutViews` facade (ADR-0003 § 7); no live container is ever returned. Two tiers:
331	
332	- **Tier H (hot; allocation-free; tagged `## @hot` for ADR-0010 `HOT-01`; scalar results or caller-owned `out`):** `room_at(section_id, x, y) -> int` (`0` = NONE; a sill px answers its `sill_room`, so no walkable point answers NONE), `floor_tile_at(...) -> int` (`-1` = NONE), `section_at(body_id, x, y) -> int` (`0` = NONE; FLOOR division), `section_offset_x/_y(section_id)`, `body_of(section_id)`, `version`, `static_version`, `leaf_version`, `changed_region_kind/_box_into`, `door_passage_into`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `leaf_obstruction_into`, `V(room_id)`, `exposed_tiles(room_id)`, and ADR-0014's `rects_in`/`solid_in` (sentinels for an unknown or discarded section are `0`/false, never an error).
333	- **Tier C (cold; may allocate; returns a freshly built immutable record or a typed `Array[Record]`):** `room_surface`, `room_boundary`, `anchor_geometry`, `subject_anchors`, `socket_plan`, `weld_offset`, `detach_preview`, `room_adjacency`, `hull_segments_near`, `loose_slots`, `hardpoints_of`, `segment_at`, `plate_positions`, `sections_of`, `route_length_px`, `south_band`, `wall_face_rows`, `template_hash`.
334	
335	**Fixed field names, orders and bounds.** Records live in `src/sim/layout/views/` as get-only `RefCounted` classes: `AnchorGeometry {kind, host_face_id, base_px_polyline (PackedInt32Array pairs), sort_origin_y, section_id}`, `RoomSurface {floor_tiles (PackedInt32Array pairs, tile id ascending), wall_faces}` (the Failure & Trail contract, section-local), `DoorPassage` (D.5 table), `RoomAdjacencyRow {room_a, room_b_or_exterior, via (DOOR|HATCH), via_id, sill_room}`, `SubjectAnchor {local_key, kind_hint, anchor_px, room_id, console_role}`. Ordering contracts: `room_adjacency` by `(room_a, via_id)`; `subject_anchors` and the slot reads by key ascending; `plate_positions` by HULL_SEGMENT node id ascending; `room_surface` by tile id; `sections_of` by `section_id`; `detach_preview` by `section_id`. `wall_face_rows` returns at most 16 rows (the Failure & Trail bound `WALL_ROWS_MAX`). Cold reads that depend only on a template (`room_adjacency`, `south_band`, `plate_positions`) are precomputed once per template in the catalog row, so a read is a copy, not a recomputation.
336	
337	**CONSOLE anchors (TR-derelict-034, re-tagged 2026-10-29).** `subject_anchors(section_id)` returns `SubjectAnchor` rows with `kind_hint` in `{DOOR_FACE, HARDPOINT, SOCKET, SLOT, CONSOLE, INSTRUMENT}`; `console_role` is `POD` or `DOCK` and is **present iff `kind_hint` is `CONSOLE`**. The structural lint `CONSOLE_ROLE_UNSET` (ERROR, boot-tier invariant) rejects a CONSOLE anchor without a role and a role on any other kind. The counts "each dock room holds exactly one dock status glow on its docked-podcraft prop" and "the world holds exactly four CONSOLE anchors" are **Derelict Authoring content lints** (`POD_CONSOLE_MISSING`, `DOCK_CONSOLE_MISSING`, the world-level count) evaluated over this read; Layout asserts no placement and counts nothing at runtime.
338	
339	**Frame rule (TR-section-039, LY-3 c).** Every geometry read answers section-local base px; the caller composes `section_offset`. Reads that answer for one body answer in the body frame. A read never mixes frames.

341	### 12. Capacity, size and world-build budgets
342	
343	- **Ceilings** are the registered constants and GDD knobs named in § 9, loaded from the `LayoutTuning` `ScalarTable` in the default-config data (ADR-0007 § 1.5); the module source contains no literal for any of them, and a start-up test runs the module at each knob's published minimum and maximum. Published ranges are guidance: an out-of-range value appears in the ADVISORY range report and is never clamped or asserted at boot; only schema bounds (`CONTENT_FIELD_RANGE`) and named structural invariants (`CONTENT_INVARIANT`: `area_max > 0`, `GRID_24`, `RECT_STRIDE_OVERFLOW`, `RECT_FLAGS_ILLEGAL`, `CONSOLE_ROLE_UNSET`, rotation 0) refuse a load (TR-section-033 Layout side).
344	- **Block size.** `bytes ~ 4 * (14 I + 10 K + 4 S + 3 B + 3)` over instance, weld, socket and body rows (D.21 with the 14th column), plus strings; `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SOFT_BYTES` raises the one-shot diagnostic `layout_block_soft_bytes`; `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES` is Save/Load's hard ceiling. The long-campaign shape (24 live and 200 tombstoned sections) is tens of KB.
345	- **World ceilings (TR-webmap-036 Layout half).** Layout supplies `V(room)` and the rect and door counts; the tile ceiling `TILES_WORLD_MVP`, the S0 to S4 loaded-set tile counts and `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` are lints and tests owned by Derelict Authoring and Web Map. A test builds the S4 loaded set through `build_section` (not a hand sum) and asserts the real `V` totals and rect counts against them. `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` (GDD Tuning Knobs) is the PROJECTOR's chunk size (ADR-0034); Layout's contribution is the per-section tile count.

347	### 13. Scene boundary and the PROJECTOR's inputs
348	
349	The Layout data module references no `Node`, `Node2D`, `TileMapLayer`, `SceneTree`, `Resource` subclass or engine physics type (AC-120); a headless run leaves the orphan-node count unchanged. The PROJECTOR (`src/presentation/projector/`, ADR-0034) is a separate subscriber that never writes a block and never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D`, builds door, prop, machinery and bead/plate/scar sprites from the rect table and `welds[]`/socket state, and redraws on `SEC`, `BODY`, `SEAM` and `LEAF` keys. This ADR guarantees the three inputs of the sprite `entity_id` are stable: `section_id` (never reused, below 2^20), a closed `kind_ordinal` vocabulary (door leaf, prop, machinery, bead, plate, scar), and `template_local_idx` (the rect `idx` or the template placement index, below the rect stride and so below 2^16). The packing function and the namespace byte `LAYOUT_ID_NS` belong to ADR-0034 and the Pipeline (OQ-33); Layout exports no packing helper and tiles carry no `entity_id`.

413	### Implementation Guidelines
414	
415	- **Must** register exactly one block (`layout.state`), one hook (`layout.doors`), one fault domain (4), one key space `{SEC 1, BODY 2, SEAM 3, LEAF 4}` and one diagnostics channel, only through `ModuleFacet.registrar` in `BOOTING`; **must never** register a second Layout block or a `layout.templates` block.
416	- **Must** store instances by reference (`template_id` plus drift hashes plus runtime fields); **must never** put geometry, a rect, a leaf, a tile list, a `kind`, a `visited` bit, a loose-item row, a door `area` or `door_state`, a float, a `layout_hash` or `mutation_count` in `layout.state`.
417	- **Must** snapshot as the § 2 closed key set of parallel columns, ascending ids, duplicated packed arrays; **must never** use an int-keyed `Dictionary`, `PackedStringArray`, `Vector2i`, `Rect2i`, `StringName` or `Resource` in the payload, and **must never** put a key in the payload that is not on the regenerated allow-list.
418	- **Must** keep `section_id == row + 1` and `body_id == row + 1`: an id is consumed only by the call that appends its row; **must never** reuse, renumber, skip or reserve an id, and **must never** let a counter wrap (the `can_*` check fails first).
419	- **Must** pass the Graph the section id and store the returned `{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}`; **must never** allocate a node, edge, compartment or seam id in Layout, and **must never** read the Graph's `next_*` counters except in the post-restore verification.
420	- **Must** compare stored hashes as `value & 0xFFFFFFFF` (`IntMath.low32`); **must never** compare a `PackedInt32Array`-read hash unmasked.
421	- **Must** compute the three template hashes once at catalog freeze with `Hash64.of_value` over the § 4 sub-payloads; **must never** write owner byte encoders for them (ADR-0005 `owner_canonical_byte_writer`) and **must never** store them in a template file.
422	- **Must** write a socket's state only inside LM2 and LM3 and choose the weld survivor by lower `body_id`; **must never** add a `set_socket_state` or `install_cap_plate` mutator, and **must never** let the result of a weld depend on argument order.
423	- **Must** begin every mutator with `scope.open_for(&"layout.state")`, check every Class A status, mark keys explicitly (`DirtyKey.make`) after the writes; **must never** rely on a packed-array property setter for dirty tracking (4.7), and **must never** call a Graph mutator from a `can_*` check.
424	- **Must** make LM2 seed each new LEAF closed with its last-projected cache and **must never** read the Graph's `area` inside LM2; **must** make `layout.doors` bump a section's `leaf_version` at most once per tick and **never** `static_version`.
425	- **Must** treat every door `area` write as a P2 write by command; **must never** call `set_opening_area` from a hook, and **must never** store, mirror or write `area` or `door_state` in Layout.

434	## Alternatives Considered
435	
436	### Alternative 1: Full geometry in the block
437	- **Description**: Each instance stores its rooms, rect table, sockets and doors in `layout.state`.
438	- **Pros**: A save is self-contained; a template edit cannot affect an old save; no catalog dependency at restore.
439	- **Cons**: Rectangles times sections times snapshot cadence bloat the block (hundreds of rects per ship against tens of rows); authored data is duplicated into every save; the Vertical Slice "seed plus deltas" model is defeated; an exporter bug is persisted forever; the hash covers authored data that is already hashed at catalog freeze.
440	- **Rejection Reason**: Instances by reference with drift hashes keeps the block at tens of KB, and the drift policy already turns a template edit into a loud restore failure where it matters.
441	
442	### Alternative 2: A second block `layout.templates`
443	- **Description**: Templates become a persisted block of their own so the save carries what it was built from.
444	- **Pros**: Restore never consults the catalog.
445	- **Cons**: A second restore root and a second hash for data that never changes at runtime; it contradicts ADR-0007's "catalogs are not state blocks"; it duplicates the content pipeline's integrity checks.
446	- **Rejection Reason**: Static data belongs to the catalog; the block stores references.
447	
448	### Alternative 3: Array-of-`Dictionary` or int-keyed `Dictionary` tables in the snapshot
449	- **Description**: One row per instance as a `Dictionary`, or a table keyed by id.
450	- **Pros**: Readable dumps; trivial lookup by id.
451	- **Cons**: JSON turns int keys into strings and numbers into floats (LY-26 a); a per-row `Dictionary` allocates and sorts per row in the encoder; ADR-0005 § 3.6 asks blocks with more than about 250 scalar fields to use packed arrays; two equal worlds reached by different histories could order differently.
452	- **Rejection Reason**: Dense parallel columns in ascending id order are the shape ADR-0005 and ADR-0006 are built for, and `id - 1` row addressing removes the lookup map.
453	
454	### Alternative 4: The Graph allocates `section_id` (and Layout asks for it)
455	- **Description**: `build_section` calls M1 first and takes the section id from the return.
456	- **Pros**: One fewer counter in Layout.
457	- **Cons**: Layout cannot name its own row, dirty key or body before the Graph runs; the `rect_key` bound (2^20) becomes the Graph's responsibility; Layout's `can_build` could not test the section-id ceiling before calling the Graph; two persisted counters would both claim to be the section counter.
458	- **Rejection Reason**: The GDD and the Graph (LS-15) already treat the section id as a caller input to M1. Layout allocates; the Graph's counter follows.
459	
460	### Alternative 5: Layout also allocates the Graph's node, edge and compartment ids
461	- **Description**: Layout hands the Graph explicit id ranges.
462	- **Pros**: `graph_ref_base` becomes Layout's alone.
463	- **Cons**: Layout would have to know the Graph's per-template node and edge counts and its capacity rules; two owners could both write the Graph's counters.
464	- **Rejection Reason**: One writer per fact; the Graph returns the bases it allocated.
465	
466	### Alternative 6: A nested ledger (one entry per template with a `room_keys` list), or two ledger spaces
467	- **Description**: `pairs[]` holds templates, each with a nested list of room keys; or `section_templates` and `section_rooms` are separate spaces.
468	- **Pros**: Mirrors the data's shape.
469	- **Cons**: A nested form needs a second `verify` and a second append-only gate (the generic one compares pairs); a per-template list makes "remove one room" a list edit instead of a per-pair `dormant` flip; two spaces mean two files and a cross-file foreign-key check.
470	- **Rejection Reason**: One flat space with compound keys reuses ADR-0007 unchanged and keeps the CI diff a list of added pairs.
471	
472	### Alternative 7: Owner-written TLV for the template hashes (ADR-LAY-06 as the GDD wrote it)
473	- **Description**: `canonical_geometry_bytes` as `[u32 tag][u32 length][payload]` in a documented field order.
474	- **Pros**: Independent of the kernel encoder.
475	- **Cons**: ADR-0005 § 3.1 forbids owner byte writers and ships golden vectors for the kernel's TLV only; a second encoder is a second injectivity argument.
476	- **Rejection Reason**: ADR-LAY-06 becomes the payload shape; the byte form is ADR-0005's.
477	
478	### Alternative 8: Two hashes only, with sets compared at restore
479	- **Description**: Keep the GDD's `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash`; classify "structural" by comparing key sets.
480	- **Pros**: The row stays 13 fields.
481	- **Cons**: There is nothing persisted to compare key sets against; a pure reorder passes every count and set and silently re-points ids to the wrong rooms and sockets.
482	- **Rejection Reason**: § 4. The third hash costs four bytes a row and makes the check exact.
483	
484	### Alternative 9: Weld survivor by argument order, or by larger body
485	- **Description**: The first argument's body survives; or the body with more sections.
486	- **Pros**: Simple call site.
487	- **Cons**: Caller mixups can dissolve the home ship and make two equal worlds hash differently; the larger-body rule changes with every weld.
488	- **Rejection Reason**: The lower `body_id` is persisted, immutable and total.

490	### Alternative 10: Derive leaves lazily on read (the GDD fallback)
491	- **Description**: No hook; a leaf is derived when a query asks, stamped by the Graph's write state.
492	- **Pros**: No P3 cost.
493	- **Cons**: A read mutates a derived cache; a refresh in P2 can precede a later same-P2 change to `area`; every consumer pays the check.
494	- **Rejection Reason**: The hook is ordered (`body.integrate after layout.doors`) and bounded; the fallback stays recorded but unused.

503	
504	### Positive
505	- One block, one owner, one closed payload shape that the type walk, the encoder and the allow-list test all agree on.
506	- Row addressing by `id - 1` removes id maps from every hot read and makes the dense-id check a restore invariant.
507	- A weld or cut gives the same bytes for the same world regardless of argument order, so `state_hash` equality and replay hold.
508	- The structural check is exact (a reorder is refused), where the GDD's wording would have corrupted old saves.
509	- Capacity ceilings fail in validate with a named reason, never as a `FAULTED` apply, and no counter can wrap.
510	- The Layout/Graph id boundary is a table; each side can be tested with the other stubbed through `LayoutGraphPort`.
511	- ADR-0014, ADR-0015, ADR-0016 and ADR-0034 build on records and rules that no longer move.
512	
513	### Negative
514	- The instance row grows to 14 columns, deviating from the TR text; the GDD, TR-section-004, D.21 and the AC-130 allow-list are updated.
515	- Dense ids forbid reserving an id; a future procgen that wants sparse or hashed ids must supersede this ADR.
516	- `layout.doors` marks a key and therefore advances `touch_serial` on door-change ticks, invalidating the block hash cache on those ticks.
517	- A new key family (LEAF) is added to a key space the GDD listed as closed.
518	- A template reorder now refuses every old save of that template (correctly, but harshly); authors must append rooms, not reorder them, once the first build is outside the project.
519	- Layout depends on a port whose Graph-side implementation does not exist yet.

521	## Risks
522	- **R1: dense-id invariant broken by a future feature.** A mutator that consumes an id without a row breaks `id == row + 1`. Mitigation: restore asserts it; a unit test builds, discards and restores and checks it; a lint `LAY-ID-01` forbids writes to the counters outside LM1 and LM3.
523	- **R2: the third hash is a deviation.** A reviewer may prefer the GDD's two. Mitigation: the reasoning is in § 4 with the failing scenario; reverting is a one-column change before any save exists.
524	- **R3: hook-marked keys and hash cache churn.** If animating doors become continuous (a stepped slide, OQ-14 c), a key per tick advances `touch_serial` every tick. Mitigation: binary doors in MVP; the cost is bounded by block size; revisit with ADR-0005 § 5.4 if continuous doors are introduced.
525	- **R4: GDScript cost of the hook and of attach/detach.** All figures are pending-spike (V2, V3). Mitigation: the fallback ladder of ADR-0010 § 9; hook early-out on a Graph change counter; attach/detach are rare P2 events.
526	- **R5: element writes without a setter (4.7).** A missed dirty mark is a stale display. Mitigation: explicit marks inside mutators, the ADR-0004 audit (`quiet_writes_allowed` false), and a per-mutator key fixture.
527	- **R6: hash collisions.** `low32` of a 64-bit hash collides at 2^-32 per pair. Mitigation: hashes are diagnostic gates, restore step (6) re-validates structure against the current template independently, and a missed geometry change on an instance with history would at worst restore with a wrong abutment that the weld-offset check of step (6) catches.
528	- **R7: the Graph port is unwritten.** If ADR-0011 returns non-contiguous ranges or an allocating `opening` read, §§ 3, 8 and 10 change. Mitigation: § Related lists the exact assumptions; ADR-0011 and this ADR are reviewed together.
529	- **R8: attach can exceed the per-body rect ceiling.** `can_attach` has no `BODY_FULL` reason. Mitigation: the MVP world is a few hundred rects against `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`; a world lint bounds the sum; OQ-1.

531	- **R10: template edits after the first outside build.** Authors can break old saves. Mitigation: the ledger flips to `SHIPPED` at the same moment; CI append-only gates; the drift policy is loud, not silent.

Forbidden: `Vector2i` and every vector or rect, `Color`, `Object`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, `NodePath`, `StringName` as a key or a value (a `StringName` is decoded as one, probed, so it must be rejected, not coerced; ADR-0003's `StringName` block ids and the in-memory staged payload keys of § 3.6 are memory-only and never enter a file, where block ids are header `String`s), and non-finite floats. I'm cross-checking ADR-0010's rules against ADR-0013, noting the one-line `@abstract class_name` form already used in ADR-0011, and reviewing shadowing rules like avoiding member names that clash with native base-class properties or methods.

I decide to actually test this myself by setting up a probe project with warnings-as-errors in project.godot, since the port signatures in ADR-0013 use non-prefixed parameter names that might trigger unused-parameter warnings depending on how the checks read module state. I also note I should check whether NARROWING_CONVERSION applies and whether any constant names like `NONE` might shadow something.

I move on to other spec issues: `BuildResult`'s sketch syntax with `class_name X extends Y:` isn't valid GDScript and would fail to parse, though it's clearly meant as illustrative pseudocode rather than literal code, so I flag it as a non-blocking note. I also confirm static factory methods like `SocketRef.make(...)` are fine, then start considering how `Array[String]` typed arrays behave with the stricter type system.

Then I check whether `bsearch` on ascending base-offset columns (like `edge_base`) could misbehave when two consecutive sections share the same base value, such as a zero-edge template — tracing through whether `bsearch(id, false) - 1` still resolves to the correct section in that edge case.

Checking the edge case with equal bases: id 8 stays unassigned until a later section with nonzero count also starts at base 8, since upper_bound-1 correctly skips the zero-count section in between. The real risk is when an earlier section holds the id but a later zero-count section shares the same base — like s1 base 5 count 3 and s2 base 8 count 0, querying id 7 should still resolve to s1 since upper_bound lands past s2's base.

This is more about graph semantics than the engine itself, so I'll set it aside and move to planning concrete probes — specifically testing binary search behavior, insert/remove_at return values, int32 wraparound with a sentinel value, and various array construction and mutation methods like append, push_back, resize, and the PackedInt32Array constructor.

I also want to probe whether var_to_bytes/bytes_to_var preserve typed Array[String] metadata through round-tripping, including nested in dictionaries, and whether assigning untyped data to a typed variable triggers errors. Separately I need to test the new @abstract class and function syntax, checking subclass override behavior and warning levels, which will require setting up a project.godot and figuring out how to register class_name without needing a full import step — probably easier to just use preload/load directly instead of relying on the global class cache.

Then there's the packed array aliasing question — testing whether clearing an array and pushing back triggers reallocation, which I can't measure directly through capacity but might infer from CowData::resize behavior in the engine source, where resizing to zero unrefs the pointer; I'm fairly confident this holds for 4.0-4.4 but unsure if a later PR added capacity/reserve semantics, so I'll mark it UNVERVIFIED but low risk. I also want to check whether Dictionary values holding typed arrays retain their type after duplicate(), and whether Array[String].assign() accepts an untyped array.
